source_ref: Class 10 Chemistry - original one-line definitions of syllabus terms. No textbook passages reproduced.

items.definition: A process in which one or more substances are converted into new substances with different properties.
The symbolic representation of a chemical reaction using formulae of reactants and products.
An equation in which the number of atoms of every element is equal on the reactant and product sides.
Mass can neither be created nor destroyed in a chemical reaction, which is why equations must be balanced.
A reaction in which two or more reactants combine to form a single product.
A reaction in which a single reactant breaks down to form two or more simpler products.
A reaction in which a more reactive element displaces a less reactive element from its compound.
A reaction in which two compounds exchange their ions to form two new compounds.
A reaction in which an insoluble solid, called a precipitate, is formed.
A reaction in which heat is released along with the formation of products.
A reaction in which heat is absorbed in order to break down the reactants.
The gain of oxygen or the loss of hydrogen by a substance in a chemical reaction.
The loss of oxygen or the gain of hydrogen by a substance in a chemical reaction.
A reaction in which oxidation and reduction take place simultaneously.
A substance that supplies oxygen to, or removes hydrogen from, another substance.
A substance that supplies hydrogen to, or removes oxygen from, another substance.
The slow eating up of metals due to the action of air, moisture or chemicals on their surface.
The oxidation of fats and oils in food that changes its smell and taste.
A substance added to food containing fats and oils to prevent their oxidation and rancidity.
A substance that changes the rate of a chemical reaction without itself being consumed.
A substance that produces hydrogen ions (H+) when dissolved in water and turns blue litmus red.
A substance that produces hydroxide ions (OH-) in water and turns red litmus blue.
A base that is soluble in water.
A substance that changes its colour or smell in acidic and basic solutions and is used to test them.
The reaction between an acid and a base to form a salt and water.
An ionic compound formed by the reaction of an acid with a base, containing a positive ion from the base and a negative ion from the acid.
A scale from 0 to 14 that measures the concentration of hydrogen ions in a solution.
An acid that ionises almost completely in water, releasing a large number of H+ ions.
An acid that ionises only partially in water.
A substance whose smell changes in acidic or basic media, such as onion or vanilla essence.
The fixed number of water molecules present in one formula unit of a crystalline salt.
A substance that absorbs moisture from air and dissolves in it to form a solution.
The property of a metal that allows it to be beaten into thin sheets.
The property of a metal that allows it to be drawn into thin wires.
The property of metals to produce a ringing sound when struck.
The arrangement of metals in order of their decreasing reactivity.
An oxide that reacts with both acids and bases to produce a salt and water.
A naturally occurring compound of a metal found in the earth's crust.
A mineral from which a metal can be extracted profitably.
The impurities such as soil, sand and rock present in an ore.
Heating an ore strongly in the absence of air, used mainly for carbonate ores.
Heating an ore strongly in the presence of excess air, used mainly for sulphide ores.
A homogeneous mixture of a metal with another metal or a non-metal.
Coating iron or steel with a thin layer of zinc to protect it from rusting.
A bond formed by the complete transfer of electrons from a metal atom to a non-metal atom.
A bond formed by the mutual sharing of electrons between two atoms.
An atom or a group of atoms that gives a carbon compound its characteristic chemical properties.
A family of organic compounds with the same functional group and similar chemical properties, in which successive members differ by a CH2 unit.
A carbon compound in which all the bonds between carbon atoms are single bonds.
A carbon compound containing at least one double or triple bond between carbon atoms.
The reaction of a carboxylic acid with an alcohol in the presence of concentrated sulphuric acid to form an ester.
The reaction of an ester with a base such as sodium hydroxide to give the salt of a carboxylic acid and an alcohol.
An aggregation of soap molecules in water in which the ionic ends remain in water and the carbon chains stay away from it.
A cleansing agent that is usually an ammonium or sulphonate salt of a long carbon chain and works in hard water.
The unique ability of carbon atoms to form bonds with other carbon atoms, giving long chains, branches and rings.
Compounds with the same molecular formula but different structural arrangements.
